atoms.reason: Confining ATOM_003 to a single dedicated assertion block is a sound, low-cost scoping decision that keeps the diff reviewable and the test of the test trivial. Mildly overlaps with ATOM_008 (block vs. named function) but the two are reconcilable. Impact is moderate since it is a structural nicety rather than coverage itself.

Consensus across A and B. Calling Get-SynthesisDepthDecision directly isolates the depth-routing unit, removing pipeline/route coupling so the assertion fails for the right reason and stays robust to upstream changes. Concrete, low-risk, and the correct testing altitude for a depth-split assertion.

penalties.name: conflict_with_ATOM_007
penalties.why: Claims plan-refinement DISCUSS coverage while ATOM_007 defers the literal обсуди/discuss-stays-Standard assertion; ambiguous as written.

atoms.reason: The core deliverable and highest-impact atom: a three-pole Standard/High-Stakes/Deep assertion in one change. Accept the intent but modify the wording. As phrased, 'covering plan-refinement DISCUSS' for the Standard pole collides with ATOM_005/ATOM_007: the current router escalates literal discuss, so a literal-keyword Standard case would be red. Rephrase to cover plan-refinement DISCUSS via a non-literal-keyword input (per ATOM_005), explicitly deferring literal-keyword matching. This resolves the major review finding and keeps the change green.

Keeping fixture text ASCII avoids PowerShell encoding/parse fragility (a real failure mode in this repo), and excluding high-risk keywords from the Standard case prevents accidental escalation by the router. Overlaps with ATOM_005 but is complementary (encoding hygiene + keyword hygiene). Sound and cheap.

Highest-scoring atom. The key correctness insight: select a Standard input free of literal обсуди/discuss/architecture markers so the assertion is green against the router as it exists today. This is exactly what reconciles ATOM_003 with ATOM_007 and prevents a self-inflicted red test. Specific, low-risk, and directly enabling.

Reusing the established Assert-True / $script:pass / $script:total / exit 1 harness plus the existing ParseFile+smoke run keeps the addition consistent with the suite and lets the file's own exit code serve as the test of the test. Minimal new surface, maximal convention adherence.

penalties.name: sequencing_reference_ambiguity
penalties.why: Pegs the deferral to 'when ATOM_004 lands', but ATOM_004 is ASCII/keyword hygiene, not a router change that would make literal discuss route to Standard.

atoms.reason: The sequencing call is correct: do not add the literal-discuss-stays-Standard hard assertion red now; it asserts future router behavior. This aligns with ATOM_005 and is the right half of the ATOM_003 conflict (resolved by amending ATOM_003, not by rejecting this). Minor penalty: the dependency it names (ATOM_004) is not the change that actually unblocks the deferred assertion, so the trigger condition is fuzzy.

Confining the change to a single new Test-DepthRoutingAssertion function is a clean, well-named scoping decision. Mild tension with ATOM_001 (inline block vs. function) but compatible — the function can wrap the assertion block. Feasible and contained; impact is structural rather than coverage-bearing.

Restricting the test to existing depth-routing functions and assertion utilities already in (or dot-sourced by) the file reinforces ATOM_002 and ATOM_006: no new dependencies, no broadened surface. Correct and low-risk; specificity slightly soft on which exact functions/utilities are intended.

Including both ParseFile validation and a smoke check gives the new test a self-check (syntactic soundness + runnable behavior), consistent with ATOM_006's 'test of the test'. Catches parse-level regressions the assertion alone would miss. Cheap and well-targeted.

Fail-loud behavior — a mismatched routing producing a hard failure with a clear message — is the property that makes the assertion worth adding; a silently-passing test gives false assurance. Strong risk reduction and impact, and directly verifiable via an intentionally mismatched input. Pairs naturally with the Assert-True/exit 1 harness of ATOM_006.
